acceptance: A backend-aware test fails if any Polars materialization in benchbox/platforms/dataframe/ (polars_df.py, and the Polars branches of unified_frame.py and expression_family.py) calls .collect( outside the single helper, including _get_first_row; non-Polars branches are not constrained

A test proves engine=in-memory reaches scalar(), get_row_count(), _get_first_row() and unified-frame Polars collects (for example by patching LazyFrame.collect and asserting the engine keyword on every call during TPC-H Q11, Q15 and Q22 at SF 0.01)

Result bundles carry requested engine, collect policy, polars version and polars-runtime-32 version (or an explicit absent marker), and mark observed execution as not captured; a fixture test covers both a pre-1.35 and a post-1.35 package layout
Requesting in-memory or streaming fails the run with an error naming the version and value when the collect signature has no engine parameter (simulated 1.0.0) or Polars rejects the value
With no engine option, run output and bundle fields other than the new metadata are unchanged on 1.44.2; existing CI is green
context: Sequenced after pvm-s0a because both edit benchbox/platforms/dataframe/polars_df.py. Evidence (HEAD d076a974d): polars_df.py:372-374 collect() uses engine="streaming" when self.streaming, otherwise bare collect(); polars_df.py:406-408 scalar() does df.collect() when lazy; tpch/dataframe_queries.py:829, 863 and 1092 call ctx.scalar. Explorer _driver_version (transformer.py:374) prefers driver_version_actual for non-DuckDB platforms.
description:
The version matrix compares three engine setups: (A) each version's default collect(), which is in-memory on 1.x and streaming on 2.0; (B) in-memory on every version, which means engine="in-memory" on 2.0; (C) engine="streaming" where supported. That only works if one setting controls every Polars materialization, and today it does not: PolarsDataFrameAdapter.scalar(), get_row_count() and _get_first_row() call collect directly, TPC-H Q11, Q15 and Q22 and several TPC-DS queries use ctx.scalar, and the Polars branches of unified_frame.py materialization collect directly.

Verified engine support (D0 probe 2026-10-07): 1.0.0 has no engine parameter and silently ignores any engine keyword; 1.12.0 and 1.22.0 reject "in-memory"/"streaming" with ValueError; 1.31.0 onward accept both; every version from 1.12 rejects unknown values.

Work:
- Add a polars-df platform option `engine` with values default, in-memory and streaming. `default` calls collect() with no engine argument, so each version uses its own default.
- Route every Polars materialization through one adapter helper that applies the option. Only Polars branches change; PySpark, DataFusion and generic branches keep their contracts.
- Fold the existing streaming flag and engine_affinity tuning into the same helper without changing their current behaviour.
- Record in the result bundle the requested engine, the collect policy actually applied (the engine argument passed, or none), the polars version, and the polars-runtime-32 version when that package is installed (it exists from 1.35.2). Observed execution (streaming fallback, intermediate materialization) is not captured and is recorded as such, never inferred.

Guardrails:
- Default behaviour is unchanged: with no option set, the calls made must equal today's on the locked version.
- If a version cannot honour the requested engine value (no `engine` parameter in the collect signature, or Polars rejects the value), fail the run with an error naming the version and value. Never fall back silently.
- No version-string branching; capability detection by signature inspection only, documented in the PR.

Review amendments (D0 2026-10-07): codex C1, C9, C10; agy A4.
